canonical_question: Is the 'decrease' in dislocation density at high temperatures (Figure 12d) observed in the post-yield regime or throughout the entire strain range?

question_variants.question: Is the 'decrease' in dislocation density at high temperatures (Figure 12d) observed in the post-yield regime or throughout the entire strain range?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text notes that dislocation density tends to decrease as temperature rises, but does not specify if this applies to the post-yield regime exclusively or the entire strain range.

answers.answer: The document states that 'As the temperature rose, the dislocation density tended to decrease.' However, it does not explicitly define whether this decrease is restricted to the post-yield regime or spans the entire strain range including elastic loading.
answers.mechanism: Enhanced dislocation mobility at high temperatures
answers.boundary_limitation: Strain range (elastic vs plastic) for density decrease not specified
evidence_spans: The primary dislocations observed were Shockley partial dislocations and stair-rod immobile dislocations.
No BCC atoms were observed in any of the three orientations, indicating that no FCC-to-BCC phase transformation occurred during tensile deformation.
The yield strength of the alloy was relatively insensitive to strain rate within the simulated range.
